title: Integrability, tail bound, and decay of the polynomial–exponential weight
statement: Let n∈ℕ and a∈ℝ with a>0. Define w(s)=(1+s)^n exp(−as) and J=∫_(0,∞) w(s) ds, using real Lebesgue measure. Then w is integrable on (0,∞), J≥0, and for all real 0≤y≤t one has ∫_y^t w(s) ds≤J(1+y)^n exp(−ay). Moreover w(y)→0 as y→+∞.
